details:
1. Project Summary

PulseRoute is an offline-first, cockpit-grade Progressive Web Application (PWA) acting as an Autonomous Digital Flight Surgeon for deep-space Artemis and Mars transit missions, where Earth communication delays reach up to 44 minutes round-trip.Rather than viewing astronaut vitals in isolation, PulseRoute performs real-time multi-sensor fusion—correlating wearable biometric streams (Astroskin 3-lead ECG, SpO₂, HRV, respiration, and skin temperature) with spacecraft life support telemetry (ECLSS pCO₂, pO₂, cabin pressure, and radiation dosimetry). Powered by a 100% deterministic clinical rule engine anchored to NASA ExMC (ICL 1.0) protocols and Open Science datasets (OSD-574, OSD-379), PulseRoute eliminates generative AI hallucination risks while distinguishing true physiological emergencies from environmental hardware faults.

Equipped with predictive cognitive fatigue indexing, SANS cephalic fluid shift tracking, optical triage, store-and-forward offline persistence, and an Earth Dual-Use Mode for remote rural clinics, PulseRoute delivers life-saving autonomous medical triage from deep space to Earth.

2. Project Details

What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

PulseRoute is an offline-first, cockpit-grade Progressive Web Application (PWA) that serves as an Autonomous Digital Flight Surgeon for cis-lunar (Artemis) and Mars transit missions, where Earth communication delays range from 3 to 44 minutes round-trip.

PulseRoute operates through a four-stage autonomous clinical pipeline:

1. 1 Hz Multi-Sensor Telemetry Fusion: Instead of evaluating human vitals in a vacuum, PulseRoute ingests and correlates two simultaneous real-time streams—wearable astronaut biometrics (Astroskin Bio-Monitor: 3-lead ECG, heart rate, SpO₂, heart rate variability, respiration rate, and skin temperature) alongside spacecraft Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) cabin sensors (pCO₂, pO₂, cabin barometric pressure, ambient temperature, humidity, and solar radiation dosimetry).

2. Deterministic Clinical Correlation Engine: Every second, pure mathematical domain engines evaluate fused sensor packets against NASA Exploration Medical Capabilities (ExMC) Integrated Clinical List (ICL 1.0) rulesets. For example, if an astronaut shows tachycardia and tachypnea, PulseRoute checks cabin pCO₂ and pO₂ before diagnosing a primary cardiac or anxiety event—accurately flagging Hypercapnia (CO₂ Scrubber Failure) or Cabin Depressurization Hypoxia when the root cause is environmental.

3. Predictive Spaceflight Countermeasures:

• Canaria Cognitive Fatigue Gauge: Computes a real-time Fatigue Index (0–100) from HRV suppression, resting heart rate drift, and cumulative sleep debt to predict high-risk performance windows before critical EVA or docking maneuvers.

• Cephalic Fluid Shift & SANS Tracker: Models microgravity headward fluid migration and optic disc edema risk over Mission Elapsed Time (MET), prescribing targeted lower-body negative pressure (LBNP) or thigh-cuff (Ani's Cuff) protocols.

• Molecular Countermeasure Recommender: Integrates NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR OSD-574 & OSD-379) transcriptomic profiles to recommend targeted antioxidant and radioprotectant countermeasures during Solar Particle Events (SPE).

• Guided Self-Assessment & Optical Triage: Enables non-physician crew members to perform structured symptom triage and camera-assisted optic/dermal inspections.

4. Offline Store-and-Forward Persistence: All clinical alerts, checklist progressions, and vital snapshots are persisted locally in IndexedDB and queued in an Earth Burst-Transmission Queue for delayed store-and-forward synchronization when deep-space orbital telemetry links reopen.

What Benefits Does It Have & What Is the Intended Impact?

• Zero-Hallucination Medical Safety: Unlike Generative AI / LLM medical assistants that can hallucinate drug dosages or fail when cloud connectivity drops, PulseRoute's clinical engine is 100% deterministic, offline-native, and auditable—every clinical alert traces directly to a published NASA ExMC protocol ID.

• Preventing Misdiagnosis via Environmental Context: By fusing ECLSS life-support data with wearable biometrics, PulseRoute prevents treating an astronaut for a medical disorder when the actual emergency is a failing spacecraft CO₂ scrubber or radiation spike.

• Empowering Non-Physician Crew: On small deep-space crews where the flight medic may be incapacitated, PulseRoute's step-by-step interactive checklists and Guided Self-Assessment Wizard allow any crew member to execute life-saving medical interventions autonomously.

• Earth Dual-Use Impact (Space-to-Earth Translation): With a single toggle in the top HUD, PulseRoute switches from Deep-Space Flight Mode to Earth Dual-Use Mode (Remote Rural Clinic/ Disaster Relief). In bandwidth-starved rural clinics, disaster zones, or subterranean rescue operations, the exact same offline store-and-forward triage architecture empowers community health workers to monitor multi-patient vitals and environmental hazards without internet access.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

• Languages & Core Framework: TypeScript (Strict Mode), React 18, HTML5, CSS3, Vite.

• Aerospace UI & Data Visualization: Tailwind CSS (high-contrast space-void theme), recharts (60 FPS sliding-window SVG/Canvas waveforms for 3-lead ECG and telemetry), lucide-react iconography, and layout-stable monospaced typography (JetBrains Mono / Fira Code).

• Offline Storage & PWA Infrastructure: Dexie.js (IndexedDB transactional storage for incident logs and delayed Earth uplink packets) and vite-plugin-pwa (Service Worker caching for 100% air-gapped operation).

• Hardware & Sensor Interfaces: Browser MediaDevices WebRTC API for live optical camera triage (with deterministic synthetic fallback for headless terminals), alongside a 1 Hz virtual hardware simulator modeling the CSA/Hexoskin Astroskin smart garment and Spacecraft ECLSS sensor bus.

• Scientific Reference Data: NASA ExMC ICL 1.0 clinical thresholds, NASA LSDA microgravity baselines, and NASA OSDR (OSD-574, OSD-379) spaceflight multi-omics datasets.

How Is the Project Creative?

1. Cross-Domain Sensor Fusion (Body + Spacecraft): Treating the spacecraft cabin and the astronaut's body as a single coupled physiological system is a paradigm shift from conventional health dashboards that only plot heart rate.

2. Interactive Judge Scenario Simulator: To make deep-space medical emergencies immediately testable during judging, we engineered an interactive Scenario Bar at the bottom of the cockpit that injects realistic multi-sensor anomalies in real time—including Nominal Orbit, CO2 Scrubber Failure, Solar Particle Event (SPE), SANS Fluid Shift, EVA Cognitive Fatigue, and Cabin Hypoxia.

3. Built-In NASA Open Science Audit Inspector: Every clinical diagnosis and baseline threshold in the UI is backed by an interactive NASA Data Attribution Modal, letting judges inspect the exact NASA OSDR accession numbers and ExMC equations powering the software.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

• Communications Blackouts & High Latency: Deep-space missions cannot rely on cloud APIs or Earth-based flight surgeons during acute emergencies. Every byte of PulseRoute runs locally in the browser with zero external network dependencies.

• Spacecraft Cockpit Human Factors: During an emergency depressurization or toxic gas leak, astronauts may be wearing pressurized gloves under dim or vibrating cabin conditions. We designed PulseRoute with a strict dark-adapted palette to eliminate glare, minimum 48 × 48 px glove-friendly touch targets, zero horizontal layout shift on rapidly ticking numbers, and progressive disclosure to prevent alarm fatigue.

• Determinism Over Probabilistic AI: In safety-critical aerospace medicine, reproducibility and traceability are non-negotiable. We decoupled our pure TypeScript clinical engines from the UI layer so every diagnostic threshold is mathematically verifiable and unit-tested.
